title: Regularized Latent Dynamics Prediction is a Strong Baseline For Behavioral Foundation Models
claim: A prediction-only objective lets learned features collapse toward high similarity during training; a simple orthogonality regularizer keeps them diverse.
layout: 1 line plot, 2 environments, solid vs dashed regularized curves, shared legend below
description: A single line chart of average cosine similarity between state representations (y-axis, 0 to 0.6) against representation-learning gradient steps (x-axis, 0 to 2M). Two environments are shown by color: purple for Cheetah and green for Pointmass. Solid lines are the unregularized baseline. Cheetah starts near 0.2, jumps sharply around 0.3M steps, and plateaus near 0.55. Pointmass rises quickly to about 0.44 and stays flat. Dashed lines show the same environments with the orthogonality regularizer (λ = 1.0). They drop almost immediately to about 0.05 and stay there. Shaded bands show standard deviation over seeds and are widest on the Cheetah baseline. The legend sits below the plot. The crop also includes part of an equation and body text above and to the left of the plot.
caption: Average Cosine similarity between staterepresentations sampled uniformly from the training dataset. Feature similarity increases over the course of training; once adding our orthogonality regularizer (with λ = 1), we obtain more diverse representations. Shaded region shows standard deviation over 4 seeds.
abstract: Behavioral Foundation Models (BFMs) produce agents with the capability to adapt to any unknown reward or task. These methods, however, are only able to produce near-optimal policies for the reward functions that are in the span of some pre-existing state features, making the choice of state features crucial to the expressivity of the BFM. As a result, BFMs are trained using a variety of complex objectives and require sufficient dataset coverage, to train task-useful spanning features. In this work, we examine the question: are these complex representation learning objectives necessary for zero-shot RL? Specifically, we revisit the objective of self-supervised next-state prediction in latent space for state feature learning, but observe that such an objective alone is prone to increasing state-feature similarity, and subsequently reducing span. We propose an approach, Regularized Latent Dynamics Prediction (RLDP), that adds a simple orthogonality regularization to maintain feature diversity and can match or surpass state-of-the-art complex representation learning methods for zero-shot RL. Furthermore, we empirically show that prior approaches perform poorly in low-coverage scenarios where RLDP still succeeds.
